questions.explanation: The word 'actually' signals that reality exceeds the prediction, so planners judge the time as less than it is — 'underestimate'. The others describe things you cannot do to a duration.

questions.prompt: Her fear of bridges was entirely ______, since she knew perfectly well they were safe.
questions.explanation: A fear held despite knowing there is no danger is one without reason, which is what 'irrational' means. A fear cannot be audible, edible or alphabetical.

questions.prompt: Language remains the greatest ______ to employment for many recently arrived immigrants.
questions.explanation: Something standing in the way of employment is an obstacle, which 'barrier' names. Nothing else listed can block access to work.

questions.prompt: Adding natural light to the workspace did much to ______ both productivity and general morale.
questions.explanation: Something that 'did much' for productivity and morale improved them, which is what 'enhance' means. 'Abolish' would remove them entirely, and neither can be translated or memorised.

questions.prompt: The inspectors were primarily concerned with the ______ of the animals kept at the facility.
questions.explanation: What inspectors check about animals is their health and treatment, which 'welfare' covers. Animals do not have an alphabet, souvenir or rehearsal.

questions.prompt: The regime tried for decades to ______ any reporting that questioned its official version of events.
questions.explanation: A regime acting against reporting that contradicts it is trying to stop that reporting, which 'suppress' means. Rehearsing, inheriting or translating the reporting would not serve that purpose.

questions.prompt: The forecast for the region's economy remained ______ despite a small rise in exports.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' signals that the small good news did not change a negative outlook, which 'gloomy' describes. A forecast cannot be edible, audible or alphabetical.

questions.prompt: Three companies now ______ the market so completely that smaller competitors cannot survive.
questions.explanation: Controlling a market to the point of excluding others is what 'dominate' means. You do not rehearse or translate a market, and inheriting one would not explain competitors failing.

questions.prompt: Only a small ______ of the funds raised actually reached the communities they were meant for.
questions.explanation: 'Of the funds' calls for a word meaning a part of a whole, which is 'portion'. The other three cannot be a quantity of money.

questions.prompt: The training programme produced dogs that were remarkably ______ even in crowded public spaces.
questions.explanation: What training produces in dogs, and what would be notable in a crowd, is that they follow commands — 'obedient'. The others describe properties training could not instil.

questions.prompt: The university hopes to ______ access to its courses by offering more of them online.
questions.explanation: Putting courses online lets more people reach them, so access is widened — 'broaden'. Access is not something you rehearse, inherit or memorise.

questions.prompt: The accounting ______ cost the firm both its reputation and most of its largest clients.
questions.explanation: Something involving accounting that destroys a firm's reputation is a public wrongdoing — a 'scandal'. None of the others would cost a firm its clients.

questions.prompt: Repeated flooding had begun to ______ the foundations of several buildings along the river.
questions.explanation: Water damaging foundations over time makes them less strong, which 'weaken' means. Foundations cannot be rehearsed, translated or memorised.

questions.prompt: She remained ______ that the original diagnosis had been wrong, despite what the specialists said.
questions.explanation: Holding a belief against expert disagreement means being firmly certain, which 'convinced' expresses. A person cannot be edible, audible or alphabetical in this sense.

questions.prompt: Careful investigative ______ brought the practice to public attention long before regulators acted.
questions.explanation: 'Investigative' and bringing something to public attention both point at reporting, which is 'journalism'. The other three are uncountable nouns that cannot investigate anything.

questions.prompt: Location was the ______ consideration when the company chose where to open its first store.
questions.explanation: The consideration that mattered most when choosing a site is the chief one, which 'prime' means. A consideration cannot be edible, audible or waterproof.

questions.prompt: Thousands of workers ______ into the city each morning from towns up to fifty kilometres away.
questions.explanation: Travelling into a city for work each morning is exactly what 'commute' means. The other verbs do not describe movement at all.

questions.prompt: Years of small successes gradually gave her the ______ to apply for a senior post.
questions.explanation: What repeated success gives someone before they attempt something harder is self-belief, which 'confidence' names. The other three are physical things that cannot be gained from success.

questions.prompt: A persistent cough was the only ______ that appeared before the illness became serious.
questions.explanation: A cough appearing before an illness worsens is a sign of that illness, which 'symptom' means. None of the others is something an illness produces.

questions.prompt: Small weekly targets seemed to ______ the team far better than a single distant deadline.
questions.explanation: Comparing two ways of getting a team to work points at encouragement, which 'motivate' means. You cannot translate, photograph or inherit a team into working harder.

questions.prompt: Very few candidates ______ both the technical skill and the patience the role requires.
questions.explanation: Having two qualities at once is what 'possess' describes here. Skill and patience are not things that can be rehearsed as a pair, and they do not dissolve or evaporate.

questions.prompt: What she achieved with almost no funding was genuinely ______ by any standard.
questions.explanation: An achievement made despite no funding is worth noticing, which 'remarkable' means. An achievement cannot be magnetic, rectangular or waterproof.

questions.prompt: The patient's ______ was slower than expected but complete within six months.
questions.explanation: Something belonging to a patient that can be slow and then complete is the return to health, which 'recovery' names. The others cannot be described as complete within six months in this sense.

questions.prompt: Access to the archive is ______ to researchers who have applied at least a month ahead.
questions.explanation: Access granted only to a particular group is restricted, which 'limited' means. Access cannot be adhesive, hollow or frozen.

questions.prompt: Critics argued that the ______ was far heavier than the offence deserved.
questions.explanation: Something weighed against an offence is the penalty for it, which 'punishment' names. The other three cannot be compared to an offence at all.

questions.prompt: The threat of closure did more to ______ the staff than any management initiative had.
questions.explanation: A shared threat bringing people together is what 'unite' describes. Staff are not laminated, photographed or memorised by a threat.

questions.prompt: The meeting felt ______, though the minutes later showed it had lasted only an hour.
questions.explanation: The contrast with 'only an hour' shows the meeting seemed to go on forever, which 'endless' means. A meeting cannot feel adhesive or frozen, and 'circular' would describe its logic rather than its length.

questions.prompt: The farm switched to ______ methods and stopped using chemical fertiliser altogether.
questions.explanation: Abandoning chemical fertiliser is exactly what 'organic' farming means. Farming methods cannot be audible, portable or alphabetical.

questions.prompt: Speaking publicly against her own employer was a ______ decision that cost her the job.
questions.explanation: Acting against your own interest at real personal cost is brave, which 'courageous' means. A decision cannot be magnetic or rectangular, and 'hollow' would describe a promise rather than a risk taken.

questions.prompt: Online sales are expected to ______ shop sales within the next three years.
questions.explanation: One figure rising past another is what 'overtake' describes. Sales cannot rehearse, laminate or memorise anything.

questions.prompt: Demand reaches its ______ in late August and falls sharply once schools reopen.
questions.explanation: A high point that demand reaches before falling is its 'peak'. None of the other options is something demand can reach.

questions.prompt: Only one ______ had any experience of managing a budget of that size.
questions.explanation: Someone being assessed for experience relevant to a role is a 'candidate'. The others are objects and cannot have experience.

questions.prompt: He was entirely ______ of the rules until someone finally showed him the handbook.
questions.explanation: Not knowing the rules until shown them is what 'ignorant of' means. A person cannot be adhesive, audible or waterproof in relation to rules.

questions.prompt: The company's ______ for the coming year improved considerably after it secured the government contract.
questions.explanation: Something 'for the coming year' that a contract improves is the expected future, which 'outlook' names. The others cannot be held for a coming year.

questions.prompt: Rising interest rates made the monthly ______ payments unaffordable for many households.
questions.explanation: Monthly payments affected by interest rates are loan repayments on a home, which 'mortgage' names. Nothing else listed involves interest.

questions.prompt: Every article is read by at least one ______ before the journal agrees to publish it.
questions.explanation: Someone of equal standing who reviews academic work before publication is a 'peer'. The other three cannot read anything.

questions.prompt: The sudden ______ of bees from the region alarmed farmers across three counties.
questions.explanation: Bees going from a region and alarming farmers describes them vanishing, which 'disappearance' names. The others cannot happen to bees.

questions.prompt: The park was designed for ______ rather than for sport, with no marked pitches at all.
questions.explanation: Set against sport, and explained by the absence of pitches, the park is for relaxed leisure — 'recreation'. A park cannot be designed for an invoice, bandage or cutlery.

questions.prompt: The ______ river that once powered every mill in the valley is now barely a stream.
questions.explanation: A river that once powered every mill was powerful, and 'now barely a stream' sharpens that contrast. A river cannot be adhesive, alphabetical or portable.

questions.prompt: The firm lost its largest ______ after missing three deadlines in a single quarter.
questions.explanation: Someone a firm can lose by missing deadlines is a customer it works for, which 'client' names. A firm does not lose staircases or melodies through poor delivery.

questions.prompt: The merger caused months of ______ before anything resembling a routine returned.
questions.explanation: Months of disruption ending when routine returns is what 'upheaval' describes. The other three cannot last for months or be caused by a merger.

questions.prompt: Conditions in the older wing were ______, and the inspectors ordered it closed immediately.
questions.explanation: Conditions bad enough to force immediate closure are shocking, which 'appalling' means. Conditions cannot be adhesive, alphabetical or portable.

questions.prompt: The guide was unusually ______ about the building's history and answered every question.
questions.explanation: Answering every question about a history means knowing a great deal, which 'knowledgeable' means. A guide cannot be magnetic, waterproof or rectangular about history.

questions.prompt: The player faced a three-match ______ following the incident in the second half.
questions.explanation: Being barred for three matches after an incident is a temporary ban, which 'suspension' names. None of the others can be measured in matches.

questions.prompt: His reply was so ______ that nobody could tell whether he actually agreed.
questions.explanation: Saying the opposite of what you mean leaves listeners unsure of your real view, which is what 'sarcastic' produces. A reply cannot be adhesive or waterproof, and 'circular' would describe faulty reasoning rather than tone.

questions.prompt: Students tend to ______ near the entrance whenever the weather turns cold.
questions.explanation: People gathering in one place is what 'congregate' means. Students do not evaporate, laminate or translate near an entrance.

questions.prompt: She had nobody at work she could ______ in about how badly things were going.
questions.explanation: The pattern 'confide in someone' means to tell them something private, which fits having nobody to talk to. The other verbs do not take 'in' with a person in this way.

questions.prompt: Critics called the policy ______, since the ministry had ignored the same rule for years.
questions.explanation: Demanding of others what you have not done yourself is what 'hypocritical' names, and the second clause supplies exactly that. A policy cannot be adhesive, rectangular or audible.

questions.prompt: Her comments on the draft were brief but unusually ______, and changed the whole argument.
questions.explanation: Brief comments that change an entire argument show deep understanding, which 'insightful' means. Comments cannot be waterproof, alphabetical or magnetic.

questions.prompt: The ______ of plant life in the reserve is greater than anywhere else in the country.
questions.explanation: A quality of plant life that can be greater in one place than another is its variety, which 'diversity' names. The others cannot describe plant life.

questions.prompt: The company found a profitable ______ supplying parts that larger manufacturers ignored.
questions.explanation: A small specialised area of a market that others overlook is a 'niche'. None of the other options can be profitable or supply parts.

questions.prompt: Only two of the twelve sites were fully ______ with the new safety regulations.
questions.explanation: Meeting regulations in full is what 'compliant with' means. Sites can be adhesive, alphabetical or portable in other contexts, but none of those relates to regulations.

questions.prompt: Without a control group the results are essentially ______, however impressive they look.
questions.explanation: Results that cannot be interpreted without a comparison carry no information, which 'meaningless' states. 'Circular' describes reasoning that assumes its conclusion, which is a different fault, and results cannot be waterproof or adhesive.

questions.prompt: The new drainage system was designed to ______ the damage caused by seasonal flooding in low-lying areas.
questions.explanation: A drainage system acts on the flooding itself, so the verb has to mean reducing the harm — that is 'mitigate'. 'Document' and 'exaggerate' describe how damage is reported rather than prevented, and nothing in the sentence suggests the damage is being delayed rather than lessened.

questions.prompt: Many small businesses remain ______ to invest in new equipment while interest rates stay high.
questions.explanation: High interest rates make borrowing costly, which explains unwillingness rather than permission or duty. 'Eligible' and 'entitled' describe a right to invest, and 'obliged' describes a requirement to — none of which the second clause would account for.

questions.prompt: Repeated delays in publishing the results began to ______ public confidence in the agency's independence.
questions.explanation: Confidence is the thing being damaged by the delays, and 'undermine' is the verb for weakening it gradually. 'Broadcast' and 'inherit' take confidence as an object in a way that makes no sense here, and you postpone an event, not a state of trust.

questions.prompt: The investigators dismissed the first theory but considered the second explanation entirely ______.
questions.explanation: 'But' sets the second explanation against a dismissed one, so the missing word must be positive about its credibility, which is what 'plausible' means. The other three describe properties an explanation can technically have but that would not contrast with being dismissed.

questions.prompt: Given how quickly the glacier has retreated, some loss of coastal habitat now seems ______.
questions.explanation: The opening clause gives a reason to expect the loss, so the word must express that it cannot be avoided. 'Optional' says the opposite, and neither 'affordable' nor 'artificial' is something the rate of glacial retreat would establish.

questions.prompt: Regulators promised to ______ every claim the company had made about the safety of its batteries.
questions.explanation: Regulators examine claims closely, which is what 'scrutinize' means. 'Publicize' would mean spreading the company's claims rather than testing them, and translating or memorizing them is not a regulatory act.

questions.prompt: The subsidy was introduced as an ______ for farmers to switch to less water-intensive crops.
questions.explanation: A subsidy is money offered to encourage a change, so it functions as an 'incentive'. 'Obstacle' reverses the effect, and neither an apology nor an exception is something you would introduce 'for farmers to switch'.

questions.prompt: If the symptoms ______ for more than a week, patients are advised to contact the clinic again.
questions.explanation: Contacting the clinic again makes sense only if the symptoms continue, which is what 'persist' means. 'Subside' and 'conclude' describe symptoms going away, which would remove the reason to call, and symptoms do not evaporate.

questions.prompt: The contract's wording was so ______ that both sides claimed it supported their position.
questions.explanation: Two sides can each claim support only if the wording admits more than one reading, which is what 'ambiguous' means. Being brief, readable or formal would not by itself allow opposing interpretations.

questions.prompt: Without regular maintenance, even well-built bridges will slowly ______ under constant traffic and weather.
questions.explanation: Lack of maintenance under constant stress causes gradual decline, which 'deteriorate' names. The other three are intransitive-looking verbs that fit the slot grammatically but describe things bridges do not do under traffic and weather.

questions.prompt: After three failed prototypes, the team finally produced a design that seemed commercially ______.
questions.explanation: 'Commercially' points at whether the design could succeed as a product, and 'viable' is the adjective for that. The others are adjectives a design could in principle carry, but none of them is something 'commercially' would modify meaningfully.

questions.prompt: Although the drug showed promise in early trials, its effect on long-term survival proved ______.
questions.explanation: 'Although' signals that the early promise was not borne out, so the effect must have been too small to matter, which is 'negligible'. 'Widespread' would describe reach rather than size and would not contrast with the promise, and an effect is not mandatory or affordable.

questions.prompt: The older instrument is slower but far more ______ than the digital version that replaced it.
questions.explanation: An instrument that can be trusted to give the same result every time is 'reliable', which is the quality the contrast with 'slower but' sets up. Courteous, fluent and apologetic all describe how a person behaves and cannot apply to a measuring instrument.

questions.prompt: A full ______ into the cause of the failure was ordered before the plant reopened.
questions.explanation: Something ordered to establish why a failure happened is a formal inquiry, which 'investigation' names. A donation, a reunion and a banquet are all events or gifts, and none of them can be carried out into a cause.

questions.prompt: Researchers recorded a steady ______ in bird numbers across the whole region over twenty years.
questions.explanation: Numbers going down gradually over twenty years is a 'decline'. A celebration, an instruction and a reminder are not quantities, so none of them can be measured in bird numbers.

questions.prompt: Given the short notice, the fee charged for the emergency repair seemed entirely ______ to us.
questions.explanation: A price that is not too high for the circumstances is 'reasonable', and the short notice is what makes it fair. A fee is a sum of money, so it cannot be coastal, musical or wooden.

questions.prompt: Regular ______ of the tunnels costs less over time than waiting for a major failure.
questions.explanation: Routine care that prevents a breakdown is 'maintenance', which is why it works out cheaper than repairing a failure. Applause, rainfall and photography do nothing to keep a tunnel in working order.

questions.prompt: A new ______ requires every supplier to report where its raw materials were produced.
questions.explanation: Something that requires companies to do a thing is an official rule, which 'regulation' names. An ornament, an aroma and a landscape have no authority and cannot require anything of anyone.

questions.prompt: The early maps were beautifully drawn but far less ______ than modern satellite surveys are.
questions.explanation: A map that matches the real world closely is 'accurate', and that is exactly what satellite surveys improve on. Being fragrant, magnetic or washable says nothing about whether a map is correct.

questions.prompt: Workers reported much greater ______ with their jobs after the company introduced flexible starting hours.
questions.explanation: The pleasure people feel about their work is 'satisfaction', which flexible hours would plausibly increase. Postage, scenery and humidity are not feelings and cannot be reported about a job in this way.

questions.prompt: Long-term ______ in the northern region fell sharply once the new rail link finally opened.
questions.explanation: The number of people without work is 'unemployment', and better transport plausibly reduces it. Architecture, cuisine and folklore are not measurable in a way that could fall when a railway opens.

questions.prompt: The thick outer shell offers the seed ______ against both drought and grazing animals.
questions.explanation: A hard shell keeps danger away from what is inside, which 'protection against' expresses. Publicity, employment and sympathy are things offered to people, and none of them defends a seed from drought.

questions.prompt: Each fossil is placed in a single ______ according to the shape of its teeth.
questions.explanation: A group that things are sorted into by a shared feature is a 'category'. An orchard, a harbour and a corridor are physical places, and nothing is assigned to them on the basis of tooth shape.

questions.prompt: There is still a wide ______ between what the theory predicts and what experiments actually show.
questions.explanation: A difference between prediction and result is a 'gap' between them. A hedge, a balcony and an avenue occupy physical space and cannot stand between a theory and an experiment.

questions.prompt: Historians treat the invention of printing as the beginning of an entirely new ______.
questions.explanation: A long period of history with its own character is an 'era', which is what historians date from printing. An appetite, an aroma and a signature cannot begin a historical period.

questions.prompt: Staff must ______ the safety officer immediately whenever a chemical container is found damaged.
questions.explanation: Telling someone about a problem straight away is what 'inform' means. You cannot embroider, refrigerate or applaud a safety officer in response to a damaged container.

questions.prompt: The quarry is owned by a ______ registered in another country and pays no local tax.
questions.explanation: A large company that can be registered abroad and hold property is a 'corporation'. A landmark, a textbook and a sculpture cannot own anything or be registered as a legal body.

questions.prompt: The long ______ of the horse can be traced through fossils found on several continents.
questions.explanation: Gradual change in a species over millions of years is its 'evolution', which is what a fossil record shows. Obedience, digestion and vocabulary leave no trace in fossils and cannot be traced across continents.

questions.prompt: Recent ______ obliges landlords to insulate any property before it can be rented out.
questions.explanation: Law passed by a parliament is 'legislation', and only law can oblige landlords to do something. Weather, furniture and traffic impose no legal duty on anyone.

questions.prompt: The chain filed for ______ after three years of losses and closed every remaining store.
questions.explanation: A business that cannot pay its debts files for 'bankruptcy', which fits three years of losses and total closure. A company cannot apply for retirement, membership or citizenship in these circumstances.

questions.prompt: Only after hours of argument did a genuine ______ emerge among the members of the committee.
questions.explanation: General agreement reached after long discussion is a 'consensus'. A fragrance, a shortage and an echo are not positions people can hold, so none of them emerges from an argument.

questions.prompt: Attendance at the safety briefing is ______ for everyone entering the laboratory, including visiting staff.
questions.explanation: Something nobody may skip is 'compulsory', which the phrase 'for everyone, including visiting staff' makes clear. Attendance is not a physical object, so it cannot be reversible, translucent or renewable.

questions.prompt: The survey is entirely ______, so no answer can ever be traced back to an individual.
questions.explanation: A survey that hides who gave each answer is 'anonymous', which is exactly what the second clause explains. Handwriting would in fact make answers easier to trace, and a survey cannot be vertical or airborne.

questions.prompt: Experts confirmed that the manuscript was ______ and not a nineteenth-century copy as some had claimed.
questions.explanation: The contrast with 'not a copy' requires a word meaning real or original, which is 'genuine'. Being illegible, bilingual or waterlogged has no bearing on whether a document is the original or a later imitation.

questions.prompt: From the tools alone archaeologists can ______ a great deal about how the settlement was organised.
questions.explanation: Working something out from indirect evidence is what 'infer' means, and tools are exactly such evidence. You cannot postpone, advertise or dismantle information about how a settlement was organised.

questions.prompt: Many early astronomers chose to ______ their entire lives to charting a single region of sky.
questions.explanation: Giving all your time and effort to one purpose is to 'devote' yourself to it. Nobody can restore, exaggerate or duplicate a life in order to spend it on a task.

questions.prompt: Any team fielding an unregistered player faces an automatic ______ of three competition points.
questions.explanation: A punishment imposed for breaking a rule is a 'penalty', and losing points is the punishment here. An upgrade, a refund and a discount are all benefits, so none of them follows from breaking a rule.

questions.prompt: The island supports at least twelve ______ of beetle found nowhere else on earth.
questions.explanation: Distinct kinds of living thing are 'species', which is what can be unique to an island. Chapters, portions and editions divide books or quantities, not populations of insects.

questions.prompt: The sudden ______ of foreign funding forced the institute to halt three long-running studies.
questions.explanation: Money being taken away is a 'withdrawal' of funding, which explains why the studies stopped. Translating, duplicating or decorating funding is meaningless and would not force research to end.

questions.prompt: Most of the objections raised at the hearing were ______ and did not affect the final decision.
questions.explanation: Objections too small to matter are 'trivial', which is why the decision was unchanged. An objection is an argument, so it cannot be metallic, nocturnal or hereditary.

questions.prompt: The risk is ______ in the method itself and cannot be removed by better training alone.
questions.explanation: A danger built into a method and impossible to train away is 'inherent' in it. A risk is not a substance or a person, so it cannot be soluble, punctual or luminous.

questions.prompt: Simple painkillers can ______ the worst of the symptoms but do nothing about the underlying cause.
questions.explanation: Making suffering less severe without curing it is what 'alleviate' means, which the contrast with the underlying cause demands. Painkillers cannot itemise, narrate or inherit symptoms.

questions.prompt: Time was the only real ______ on the project, since money and staff were both plentiful.
questions.explanation: A limit on what a project can do is a 'constraint' on it, and the second clause rules out the other two possible limits. A tribute, a verdict and a postscript place no restriction on how work proceeds.

questions.prompt: Repeated errors in the earlier report damaged the author's ______ long before the final version appeared.
questions.explanation: Mistakes make readers less willing to believe a writer, and that trust is 'credibility'. Errors in a report cannot damage an author's eyesight, handwriting or posture.

questions.prompt: Heavy editing tended to ______ rather than clarify what the original writer had actually meant.
questions.explanation: The contrast with 'clarify' calls for a verb meaning to make harder to understand, which is 'obscure'. Celebrating, italicising or punctuating a meaning is not the opposite of clarifying it.

questions.prompt: The applause was entirely ______, since nobody had arranged for the audience to react that way.
questions.explanation: A reaction that happens by itself with no planning is 'spontaneous', which the second clause spells out. Applause is a sound made by people and cannot be nutritional, microscopic or aquatic.

questions.prompt: Copying thousands of figures by hand was ______ work that nobody in the department volunteered for.
questions.explanation: Long, repetitive work that people avoid is 'tedious'. Copying figures at a desk is not seasonal, aerial or ceremonial, so none of those explains why nobody wanted the job.

questions.prompt: A single inspector was appointed to ______ every stage of the building work in the district.
questions.explanation: Watching over work to make sure it is done properly is what an inspector does, and 'oversee' names it. An inspector is not appointed to demolish, illustrate or publicise the stages of a building project.

questions.prompt: Poor ______ of air in the deep mine allowed dust to build up to dangerous levels.
questions.explanation: Air that does not move around freely has poor 'circulation', which is why dust collects. Air cannot have ownership, pronunciation or cultivation, so none of the others explains the build-up.

questions.prompt: A slight ______ between the two sets of measurements grew larger with every additional trial.
questions.explanation: Two results moving steadily further apart show a growing 'divergence' between them. Sets of measurements cannot form a partnership, exchange a handshake or develop a rivalry.

questions.prompt: The coating proved surprisingly ______, surviving ten winters without cracking or losing its colour.
questions.explanation: Something that lasts for years without damage is 'durable', which the ten winters demonstrate. Surviving winters intact says nothing about whether a coating is talkative, aromatic or buoyant.

questions.prompt: Permits granted under the old system will ______ at the end of next month without exception.
questions.explanation: A document that stops being valid on a fixed date is said to 'expire'. Hibernating, germinating and migrating are things living creatures and plants do, not official permits.

questions.prompt: Most participants felt the extra hours of study had been ______ once the results appeared.
questions.explanation: Effort that turns out to have been worth making is 'worthwhile', which is what good results show. Hours of study cannot be identical to nothing in particular, confidential, or circular.

questions.prompt: The argument fails not because the evidence is weak but because its ______ is faulty.
questions.explanation: The way reasoning moves from evidence to conclusion is its 'logic', and that is the alternative fault the sentence offers. Binding, packaging and lighting belong to physical objects, not to an argument.

questions.prompt: There is no ______ answer yet, since the last set of results has not arrived.
questions.explanation: An answer that is certain and settled is 'definite', and missing results are exactly what prevent certainty. An answer cannot be muscular, orchestral or granular.

questions.prompt: The heat inside the furnace is so ______ that the sensors must be replaced monthly.
questions.explanation: Heat strong enough to destroy equipment every month is 'intense'. Heat is a physical condition and cannot be fictional, polite or rural.

questions.prompt: Water ______ in the city fell by a fifth after the new pricing scheme began.
questions.explanation: How much water people consume is 'usage', and that is the one thing a change in price would affect. Temperature, hardness and clarity are real properties of water, but none of them responds to a pricing scheme.

questions.prompt: The building has almost no ______, so equipment is left standing in the corridors overnight.
questions.explanation: Space to put things away is 'storage', and its absence is what leaves equipment in the corridors. Ventilation, signage and insulation are also features a building may lack, but none of them would force equipment into a corridor.

questions.prompt: The ______ of the wall was reduced so that residents behind it could see the river.
questions.explanation: Only lowering how tall the wall is lets people see over it, and that measurement is its 'height'. Reducing the wall's thickness, weight or cost would leave the view blocked exactly as before.

questions.prompt: A single counter-example is enough to ______ that the rule cannot hold in every case.
questions.explanation: Evidence that settles a question beyond doubt is enough to 'prove' the point. A counter-example cannot forget, promise or regret anything, since those describe what people do.

questions.prompt: The expedition was regarded as a ______ despite the loss of most of its equipment.
questions.explanation: A great success achieved in spite of difficulty is a 'triumph', which the word 'despite' sets up. Losing equipment does not make an expedition a formality, a coincidence or a postponement.

questions.prompt: The report found clear evidence of ______ against older applicants at every stage of hiring.
questions.explanation: Treating one group worse because of who they are is 'discrimination', and the word 'against' points to unfair treatment. Gratitude, flattery and generosity are all favourable, so none of them can be directed against applicants.

questions.prompt: A ______ working day at the station involves three hours of observation and four of analysis.
questions.explanation: A day that shows the usual pattern is a 'typical' one, which is why the hours can be listed. A working day cannot be reversible, hollow or fluent.

questions.prompt: Offering to pay for the repairs was a generous ______ that the neighbours did not expect.
questions.explanation: An action done to show goodwill is a 'gesture'. A receipt, an estimate and an invoice are documents produced in the course of paying for repairs, and a document cannot itself be generous.

questions.prompt: Feeding the animals at the same hour each day quickly became an unbreakable ______.
questions.explanation: A fixed pattern repeated at the same time every day is a 'routine'. An alibi, a promise and a silence are not repeated activities, so none of them is what daily feeding becomes.

questions.prompt: The ______ recalled every unit sold that year after a fault appeared in the wiring.
questions.explanation: The company that builds a product is the 'manufacturer', and only it can recall what it sold. A spectator, a librarian and a biographer have no connection with producing or withdrawing wired units.

questions.prompt: The ______ against the treasurer was investigated for six months and finally dismissed for lack of evidence.
questions.explanation: An unproved claim that someone has done wrong is an 'allegation', which is what gets investigated and then dismissed. A nomination, an invitation and a renovation cannot be made against a person.

questions.prompt: Public ______ to the new proposal was far angrier than the ministry had ever anticipated.
questions.explanation: The way people respond to something is their 'reaction', and only a response can be described as angry. Obedience, attendance and subscription are forms of cooperation and cannot carry anger.

questions.prompt: The little-known theory gained sudden ______ after two independent laboratories confirmed its central prediction.
questions.explanation: Becoming widely noticed and important is gaining 'prominence', which contrasts with 'little-known'. A theory has no fluency, humidity or elasticity to gain.

questions.prompt: The rent was ______ rather than real, amounting to one coin handed to the landlord each year.
questions.explanation: A payment that stands for something instead of covering a real cost is 'symbolic', as a single coin shows. A rent cannot be electronic in contrast to real, and it cannot be decorative or musical at all.

questions.prompt: Rather than a fixed list, the system uses a ______ model that updates as new data arrives.
questions.explanation: A model that keeps changing in response to new information is 'dynamic', which is the opposite of the fixed list. Something printed, wooden or framed is by nature unable to update itself.

questions.prompt: The laboratory struggled to ______ enough volunteers for a trial lasting three whole years.
questions.explanation: Persuading people to join a study is to 'recruit' them, and a long trial makes that hard. Photographing, impersonating or congratulating volunteers would not fill the places on a trial.

questions.prompt: The environmental agency can ______ any company that knowingly conceals a spill from the regulator.
questions.explanation: Taking a wrongdoer to court is to 'prosecute' them, which is the power an agency holds over concealment. Reimbursing, advertising or relocating a company is not a penalty for hiding a spill.

questions.prompt: Whole districts faced ______ that winter when the harvest failed for a third successive year.
questions.explanation: Having no food to eat after repeated crop failure is 'starvation'. Taxation, conscription and quarantine are all things a population can face, but none of them follows from a failed harvest.

questions.prompt: Two managers were dismissed for ______ after auditors traced invoices to companies that did not exist.
questions.explanation: Inventing companies in order to issue false invoices is deliberate deception for money, which 'fraud' names. Lateness, absence and plagiarism are also grounds for dismissal, but none of them involves fake invoices.

questions.prompt: A proper ______ of the programme will take at least two years of careful measurement.
questions.explanation: Judging how well something works, using measurement, is an 'evaluation' of it. A celebration, an abbreviation and an illustration require no measurement and would not take two years.

questions.prompt: What began as a minor leak became a ______ that closed the plant for two years.
questions.explanation: A disaster serious enough to shut a plant for two years is a 'catastrophe', which contrasts with 'minor leak'. A curiosity, a tradition and a bargain would give nobody a reason to close anything.

questions.prompt: Her performance of the difficult passage was ______, and the recording needed no editing at all.
questions.explanation: A performance with no mistakes in it is 'flawless', which is why no editing was needed. A recording that was inaudible, unfinished or shortened would need more work, not less.

questions.prompt: A tool with no ______ will not sell, however beautiful its designer has managed to make it.
questions.explanation: Usefulness is what a tool has to have, and 'utility' names it; the contrast with beauty confirms this. Nobody buys or refuses a tool on the basis of its fragrance, vocabulary or rhythm.

questions.prompt: Strict ______ to the house style was expected of every contributor to the new journal.
questions.explanation: Following a set of rules exactly is 'conformity' to them, which is what a house style demands. A journal would not require strict objection, indifference or exposure to its own style.

questions.prompt: He had grown so ______ that he assumed every act of generosity concealed a private motive.
questions.explanation: Believing that people always act from selfish motives is being 'cynical'. Someone forgetful, sentimental or prosperous would have no particular reason to suspect hidden motives behind generosity.

questions.prompt: Her knowledge of the subject proved ______, collapsing as soon as anyone asked a detailed question.
questions.explanation: Knowledge that goes no deeper than the surface is 'superficial', which is why detail destroys it. Encyclopaedic knowledge would survive detailed questions, and knowledge that failed under questioning is not shown to be hereditary or confidential.

questions.prompt: Thick fog continued to ______ the rescue effort for several hours after the accident.
questions.explanation: Getting in the way of an operation and slowing it down is to 'impede' it, which is what fog does. Fog cannot illuminate, finance or commemorate a rescue.

questions.prompt: The ______ of a second failure rises sharply once a component has been repaired twice.
questions.explanation: How probable something is constitutes its 'likelihood', and repeated repairs make a further breakdown more probable. A failure has no colour, symmetry or texture that could rise.

questions.prompt: One ______ exception is the desert species, which survives without drinking any water at all.
questions.explanation: An exception striking enough to be worth mentioning is a 'notable' one. An animal that never drinks is not a numerical, grammatical or hourly exception to anything.

questions.prompt: Most of the land came to her as an ______ rather than through any purchase of her own.
questions.explanation: Property received from someone who has died is an 'inheritance', which is the alternative to buying it. Land does not arrive as an apology, an afterthought or an achievement.

questions.prompt: Certain smells can ______ a childhood memory more sharply than any photograph ever manages to.
questions.explanation: Bringing a memory vividly to mind is what 'evoke' means, and the comparison with photographs confirms it. A smell cannot decorate, purchase or rehearse a memory.

questions.prompt: Direct sunlight will slowly ______ the plastic until it becomes brittle and breaks apart completely.
questions.explanation: Breaking a material down over time so that it weakens is to 'degrade' it, which the brittleness demonstrates. Polishing, magnetising or laminating plastic would not leave it falling to pieces.

questions.prompt: Planners tested a worst-case ______ in which every supplier failed during the same week.
questions.explanation: An imagined sequence of events used for planning is a 'scenario', and the relative clause describes one. An ornament, an inventory and a portrait are objects or lists, and events cannot happen inside them.

questions.prompt: The old quarter has recovered much of its ______, with new shops opening every month.
questions.explanation: Energy and liveliness are 'vitality', which new shops every month demonstrate. Recovering silence, obscurity or flatness would mean the opposite of a district coming back to life.

questions.prompt: Engineers had to ______ the two halves of the tunnel to within a few millimetres.
questions.explanation: Bringing two parts into exactly the right position relative to each other is to 'align' them, which the millimetre tolerance requires. Insulating, ventilating and flooding a tunnel are not measured as a matter of alignment.

questions.prompt: The objection was purely ______: the bridge worked perfectly but many residents found it ugly.
questions.explanation: An objection about how something looks is an 'aesthetic' one, which the word 'ugly' makes explicit. The bridge working perfectly rules out a technical complaint, and nothing in the sentence concerns money or law.
